summary: The Orioles finished 2026 at 79-82 (.491), fourth in the AL East, 18.5 games behind the division-champion Rays, and missed the postseason, finishing 4.5 games out of the last AL Wild Card spot. They scored 718 runs and allowed 739 (a -21 run differential, which projects to about 78-83 by the Pythagorean formula). The high-water mark came on Apr 13 at 9-7 (+2 vs .500); the low point was 39-48 on Jun 30, and they were still at .500 (69-69) as late as Aug 31. July was the best month (15-8) and June the worst (11-16). The longest winning streak was 7 games (Jul 9–Jul 19) and the longest skid 6 (Sep 1–Sep 6). They went 18-24 in one-run games, 39-42 at home and 40-40 on the road. Pete Alonso led the club with 43 home runs and 113 RBI; Trevor Rogers posted the best qualified ERA (4.03) and led the staff with 157 strikeouts, and Andrew Kittredge led in saves (11).

sections.heading: Layoffs follow-up · GM search
bullets: Layoffs follow-up: The Athletic (via Camden Chat) puts the business-side cuts at **24+ people**, including the performers behind **the Oriole Bird and Mr. Splash**. Also cut: the team photographer and people in ticket sales, graphic design and food & beverage. No official reason has been given.

GM search: Interviews are ramping up this week, though **no names yet**. The pool includes up-and-coming player-development leaders from other organizations and at least one candidate with both MLB playing and executive experience. The O's could hire more than one executive. The lockout looms Dec 1.

sections.heading: Business-side layoffs · GM search still open
bullets: Business-side layoffs (Tue): The Banner and the Sun report cuts in business operations, content production and in-game presentation; the Sun's source says "around a dozen, if not more." The cuts were reportedly not tied to the expected December lockout. Business president Catie Griggs's memo said no further staff changes are expected.
GM search: There are **no candidate names and no hire**. Elias's search is still open, and earlier targets Kantrovitz and Barfield declined.

sections.heading: Quiet · crowded 2027 infield commentary
bullets: Quiet. **No moves and no GM-search names.** Monday coverage was commentary on a crowded 2027 infield: Westburg returning alongside Mayo, Alexander, Encarnación-Strand and Holliday.

sections.heading: No moves · FO / defense focus context
bullets: No moves on Oct 4. Context: Elias's Sept 28 end-of-season comments are still being written up (GM search reopened, bigger front office, Mejdal and Blood changes). MLBTR (Oct 3) says defense, especially the outfield, is an offseason focus.

sections.heading: Finale canceled (rain)
bullets: Canceled (rain). Sustained rain; canceled ~three hours after scheduled 1:05pm ET start; no lineup announced. Yankees finish 93–67; host AL Wild Card vs Boston. **Orioles finish 79–82** under first-year manager Craig Albernaz. First time since 2002 Yankees didn’t play all 162 in a non-shortened season (Elias via AP/ESPN).
